Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

📅 29 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4144 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?
  • It is notable, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate.
  • Recent findings suggest that but the penalty that changed the contest?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is notable, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

Recent findings suggest that but the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a significant day needed to see but this was reality.

Sources indicate that alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw.

In a recent development, “I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola mentioned. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

Sources indicate that “I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”.

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd.

Industry observers note that he did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola stated with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”.

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

Sources indicate that they had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm.

According to recent reports, “There were many positive aspects,” mentioned Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”.

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX.

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m.

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6.

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI.

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es.

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Recent findings suggest that munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ.

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

It has been revealed that iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister. Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Industry observers note that amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

It has been revealed that andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

In a recent development, the Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Sources indicate that gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw.

Sources indicate that delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob.

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

Sources indicate that so much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

It has been revealed that isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB.

Recent findings suggest that wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

In a recent development, there is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

In a recent development, jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

Industry observers note that you can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

Industry observers note that it’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW.

In a recent development, forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

Sources indicate that what a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU.

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

In a recent development, liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

It has been revealed that sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

According to recent reports, for the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

In a recent development, ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm.

According to recent reports, liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Sources indicate that huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F.

Sources indicate that van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

It has been revealed that ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that the hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

Industry observers note that A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as massive call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

Industry observers note that A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Sources indicate that anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7.

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW.

Warm-ups. ✔️ pic.twitter.com/viTAI5FqaQ.

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group confirmed they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”.

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially major-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk.

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd.

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another major-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

Liverpool: Alisson, Frimpong, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Szoboszlai, Mac Allister, Munoz, Wirtz, Gakpo, Isak.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Araujo, Gravenberch, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Having only joined up with his teammates a couple of days ago, fresh signing Liam Delap begins his Nottingham Forest career on the bench, with Igor Jesus preferred as the central striker.

Industry observers note that lining up at Liverpool. 📋 pic.twitter.com/1gtQ7BQz5J.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola has made two changes to the side that drew with Newcastle United. Victor Munoz starts with Rio Ngumoha on the bench. The other alteration sees Alexis Mac Allister replace Ryan Gravenberch in midfield.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

Sources indicate that the former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of significant-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

In a recent development, both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

In a recent development, feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

According to recent reports, goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

Fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

ADO Den Haag 3-1 Sparta Rotterdam.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 2-5 PSV Eindhoven.

It has been revealed that are you the most knowledgeable football fan around? Do you want to be involved with EA SPORTS FIFA? Well, you’re in luck as the FIFA Talent Scout team is looking for people like you.

The FIFA Talent Scout community has over 6000 active members and is always looking for individuals to help improve their football database.

This is a great opportunity to put your knowledge of your club to good use, helping to ensure that the EA SPORTS football database continues to contain the most up to date and accurate team and player data for the many leagues featured in FIFA 17.

Recent findings suggest that the first step into our community is as a football analyst, who can examine team and player data and offer feedback suggesting possible changes. You can contribute towards improving player appearance, player attributes, team formations and team tactics. There is no minimum or maximum expectation in terms of your contribution to the database. The key is that when you do contribute, your feedback helps to improve the authenticity of FIFA 17.

Those who stand out may be offered the chance to join our editing team and the chance to take full responsibility for a team and its squad. We are able to offer some financial compensation to editors, but in return we do require that you are a very active contributor who works to our deadlines and in line with our guidelines.

#3045. £380m = zero points: Substantial-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

📅 29 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 24m • 📚 Deep Dive (4837 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

£380m = zero points: Substantial-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

📅 29 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see.
  • Recent findings suggest that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net.
  • According to recent reports, this meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight upcoming signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

Recent findings suggest that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

According to recent reports, this meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

According to recent reports, it proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined plan, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” said Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

For Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

In a recent development, de Zerbi said he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”.

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH.

Newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY.

In a recent development, “After the first goal we lost confidence,” remarked De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”.

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five fresh arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA.

Industry observers note that might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

According to recent reports, there are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

According to recent reports, at least the challenges facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too significant. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

“At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach said: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match strategy at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

According to recent reports, “We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

"With the fans behind us, no one can stop us" 🖤Yoane Wissa reacts to Newcastle's win at Spurs! pic.twitter.com/itaiVO3Kx1.

After a tumultuous summer, Jaissle has ushered in a upcoming era of hope and positivity at Newcastle, with Wissa and Elanga reborn in attack.

"Oh Jaissle, I can boogie..." 🎶🕺 pic.twitter.com/FmvC2DrLMO.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Recent findings suggest that despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in latest boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Sources indicate that newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

In a new feature PortuGOAL will be bringing you some recommended reading about Portuguese football from around the web, penned by our own network of writers or others.

Industry observers note that we kick off by alerting you to a superb interview in the Guardian by Nick Ames with Port Vale's Portuguese manager Bruno Ribeiro. It has been revealed that benfica are top of the Liga NOS and their coach Rui Vitória continues to confound the doubters who believed he would not be up to the job at the Lisbon giants. Simon Curtis takes a look at "the quiet man at the helm of a national institution". And Benfica fans, while we've got your attention, a shout out for Tom Kundert's profile of the club's world-renowned Seixal Academy for ESPN.

Talking about Portuguese football schools, none has produced more top-class players in recent decades than Sporting's Alcochete Academy, and the excellent Outside of the Boot website has a brilliantly detailed profile written by Mateus Carvalho of another possible gem for the Lions, Francisco Geraldes, who is presently on loan at Moreirense.

Industry observers note that to finish up this initial trip around the net, we alert you to FourFourTwo's list of the 59 best Under-21 footballers from around the world. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, après le carton de son livre Foot Sentimental paru il y a 3 ans aux éditions Le Cherche midi, Dominique Rocheteau a fait paraître le mois dernier dans la même maison Soif d'Idéal. L'Ange Vert revient dans ce bouquin - anecdotes à l'appui - sur la Rocheteaumania qui a envahi la France après le mythique quart de finale retour de Coupe d'Europe des Clubs Champions qui s'est déroulé le 17 mars 1976 dans le Chaudron. Extraits.

"C'est seulement le lendemain de notre victoire contre Kiev, puis dans les jours qui ont suivi, que j'ai commencé à prendre la mesure de ce qui venait de se passer. Peu à peu, j'ai perçu l'ampleur de cette vague verte qui n'allait cesser de grandir, et de ce que ce match allait changer dans ma vie. À l'entraînement, une foule que je n'avais encore jamais vue pour un simple décrassage nous attendait : à l'entrée, à la sortie, tout autour du terrain. Que du vert. Cette fois, j'ai pu saluer mes parents à la sortie du stade, juste avant qu'ils ne reprennent la route. J’étais heureux, bien sûr, mais je l'avoue un peu perdu, déconcerté, face à cet engouement auquel je n'étais absolument pas préparé.

J'ai vraiment pris conscience que quelque chose avait changé lors de nos déplacements en championnat après Kiev. C'était comme si toute la France était derrière nous. Et puis, il y avait les médias, plus seulement sportifs : Paris Match, Télé 7 Jours, Rock & Folk, Rolling Stones, Salut les copains, Pif Gadget… Je ne lisais pas les journaux, je ne regardais pas la télévision. J'étais un peu dans mon monde, mais désormais je devais « apprendre » à me raconter. J'acceptais les demandes, plus par politesse que par réelle envie. Je me retrouvais souvent pris de court, parfois même paniqué. Je n'avais pas d'agent. Les journalistes passaient par le club pour leurs demandes d'interview, et je me sentais obligé d'accepter. À 20 ans, je ne contrôlais rien. Un jour, je me suis rendu compte que j'avais donné une interview pour un magazine érotique… quand ils m'ont envoyé le numéro. C'est aussi après Kiev que l'on a commencé à m'appeler l’« Ange vert », un surnom que j'ai mis du temps à apprécier.

Sources indicate that ce qui m'a le plus désarçonné, ce sont ces sacs de courriers qui ont commencé à arriver. Que faire de tout ça ? Je lisais quelques lettres, mais il y en avait des milliers. Il y avait de tout : des demandes en mariage, des déclarations d'amour, des confidences, des photos, des messages, comme si nous nous connaissions depuis toujours. Après les vacances d'été et celles de Noël, quand je revenais de Charente-Maritime, le secrétaire de l'AS Saint-Étienne m'invitait à passer récupérer au stade des sacs postaux. « Il y en a plusieurs kilos ». Je devinais à son ton que cela représentait une charge de travail. Ils étaient remplis de lettres et parfois de cassettes audio de filles envoyant des compliments ou des messages, par exemple : « Dominique, j'aimerais bien que l'on se voit ». Certaines glissaient même un chewing-gum à l'intérieur. Beaucoup de lettres venaient de filles. Certaines m'avouaient qu'elles m'aimaient.

It has been revealed that il y avait aussi des plaisanteries comme cette lettre émanant de lycéennes d'un établissement religieux en région parisienne qui suggérait mon mariage avec une fille « de bonne famille » de leur entourage. D'autres donnaient des recettes miracles pour faire cesser les rhumes ou bien améliorer le tonus. Des collégiens racontaient aussi le plaisir qu'ils avaient à chanter pendant leurs cours la chanson « Allez les Verts » pour embêter leurs professeurs. Beaucoup de lettres venaient d'Afrique, où Saint-Étienne était très aimé. Certaines étaient longues, parfois plusieurs pages et vraiment très belles. Mais aussi des pays de l'Est -Pologne, Allemagne de l'Est, Tchécoslovaquie - d'où de nombreux collectionneurs m'envoyaient des photos parues dans les magazines afin que je les signe. J'en reçois encore aujourd'hui au siège du club qui me les fait suivre à chaque fois.

Mes amis Hugues et Louis - qui habitait à Saint-Héand et préparait son concours du barreau - et moi, nous nous asseyions par terre dans la salle à manger pour trier le courrier. Impossible de répondre à tout le monde. Nous envoyions une photo dédicacée à ceux qui avaient joint une enveloppe timbrée à leur nom. Certains glissaient même un billet de 20 ou 50 francs pour recevoir une photo signée. Nous remettions ensuite les enveloppes à la postière de Saint-Héand qui nous félicitait : « Joli travail ! », avant de les oblitérer. À travers toutes ces petites histoires, j'étais à la fois touché mais aussi terriblement gêné. Tout cela me paraissait énorme, démesuré. Dans la rue, j'appréciais les marques de sympathie même si elles me mettaient mal à l'aise. Je ne savais pas toujours quoi dire, alors je répondais par un sourire.

Un matin de juillet 1976, j'étais en vacances chez mes parents. Je dormais encore tandis que ma mère et Louis prenaient le café dans le jardin. Un jeune homme s'est présenté derrière le grillage et a demandé à me voir. Ma mère lui a demandé s'il me connaissait. Devant sa réponse affirmative et son insistance, elle a fini par le laisser entrer. Ils sont venus me réveiller. « Il y a un ami qui veut te voir ». Je me suis levé, surpris. « Je ne vous connais pas » -  « Si, je vous ai vu à un match »… « Qu'est-ce que vous voulez ? » « Un autographe ». Je me suis exécuté et il est reparti ravi. Je suis resté partagé entre la satisfaction de faire plaisir et le malaise de voir ma vie privée ainsi envahie.

Une autre fois, peu après avoir fait construire mon chalet à La Gimont, je suis rentré de l'entraînement et j'ai constaté que mon chat, Diamant, avait disparu. Une femme était venue chez moi, l'avait emmenée et avait fait savoir à mon entourage que si je voulais le récupérer, je devais me rendre personnellement chez elle à Veauche, à une dizaine de kilomètres. Mon ami Louis a tenté de la raisonner, en vain. Que faire ? Il n'était pas question pour moi de céder à ce chantage. Je ne voulais pas y aller, mais je tenais à récupérer mon chat. Yves, le frère de Louis, a alors appelé la gendarmerie de Saint-Galmier. Les gendarmes se sont rendus à Veauche et ont réussi à convaincre la dame de rendre Diamant. Ils n'ont toutefois pas pu le ramener eux-mêmes. Sur leur conseil, Louis a sauté dans sa voiture pour aller le chercher. Quand il est arrivé, le chat était couché sur un coussin, sur une chaise. La femme lui a lancé : « Voyez, il avait déjà pris ses marques. » Grâce à Louis et à l'intervention des gendarmes, j'ai pu récupérer Diamant et une fois de plus mesurer la chance que j'avais d'avoir des amis en or. 1976 a été une année folle. Depuis Kiev, tout avait changé autour de moi, mais je n'ai jamais vraiment cherché à me protéger ni à mettre de la distance entre moi et les autres. Je voulais simplement vivre une vie normale, comme les autres jeunes de mon époque.".

This Just Giving page is a simple way for people, wherever they are in the world, to make a contribution to help rebuild these communities and bring some comfort to those who lost everything in the blink of an eye. The money raised will be sent to a network of local authorities and charities working in the area affected. Thank you for your support.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La retraite internationale de Romelu Lukaku (33 ans), meilleur buteur de l'histoire en sélection belge (94 pions en 135 sélections), laisse un grand vide chez les Diables Rouges. Comme l'a souligné hier La Dernière Heure Les Sports +, les candidats ne manquent pas mais le Diablotin Lucas Stassin part de loin. Extraits.

"Charles De Ketelaere a pris le relais, dans un autre style mais sans être remis en question. Il est le titulaire incontesté en pointe, même s'il joue à une autre position à l'Atalanta. Il sera d'ailleurs intéressant de voir s'il osera prendre le n°9 au prochain rassemblement. Qui pour doubler CDK dorénavant ? Le casting est large et étonnamment ouvert.

In a recent development, loïs Openda peut y penser, lui qui retrouvait peu à peu ses sensations à Lyon avant de se blesser et de manquer ce rassemblement. Mais parviendra-t-il enfin à éclore en équipe nationale alors qu'il fêtera bientôt son 27e anniversaire ? Il n'a inscrit que trois buts chez les Diables jusqu'à présent.

Hugo Cuypers, le Belge le plus prolifique ces derniers mois, peut espérer monter en grade après avoir fêté sa première sélection. Mais lui aura 30 ans au prochain rassemblement. Il ne sera pas une solution à long terme et devra aussi prouver qu'il peut avoir le niveau en évoluant dans le championnat mexicain.

L'avant-centre le plus prometteur en Belgique, c'est probablement Matias Fernandez-Pardo (21 ans), mais avec un tout autre profil que Lukaku et De Ketelaere. Acheté 60 M€ par Newcastle cet été, il possède une vitesse et une puissance de jambes assez phénoménales. Le tout avec un vrai sens du but.

Le sélectionneur a aussi une autre option, très différente : le faux 9. Deux joueurs sont capables de prendre ce rôle, que CDK peut parfois avoir selon le moment du match. On pense à Leandro Trossard, qui avait par moments dépanné Arsenal devant, et à Mika Godts, barré sur les flancs par Jeremy Doku et Diego Moreira. Lui aussi a déjà évolué en faux 9, à l'Ajax.

It has been revealed that L'idée sera aussi de regarder dans le réservoir belge. En Espoirs, trois attaquants prouvent qu'ils ont des qualités : Lucas Stassin, Romeo Vermant et Norman Bassette. À tel point que le coach Gill Swerts a cherché un système pour en utiliser au moins deux des trois en même temps. Leur évolution en club fera beaucoup de leur avenir à court terme chez les Diables.".

Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

📅 30 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.
  • It has been revealed that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five.
  • But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

It has been revealed that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”.

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Sources indicate that jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso stated. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”.

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0.

Sources indicate that "Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl.

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez remarked. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

According to recent reports, conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was rapidly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

It has been revealed that “We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”.

Chelsea’s upcoming set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, mentioned his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they revealed it in certain moments of the game.”.

Recent findings suggest that palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro indicates he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert.

According to recent reports, 6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D.

September 5: Brighton vs Leeds (Premier League)September 13: Coventry vs Brighton (Premier League)September 16: Manchester United vs Brighton (League Cup)September 19: Brighton vs Arsenal (Premier League)October 10: Sunderland vs Brighton (Premier League).

September 6: Arsenal vs Chelsea (Premier League)September 9: Chelsea vs Leeds (League Cup)September 12: Chelsea vs Hull (Premier League)September 18: Brentford vs Chelsea (Premier League)October 10: Chelsea vs Bournemouth (Premier League).

Sources indicate that the final game of the day comes from the north west as Manchester United host newly-promoted Ipswich. That game kicks off at 4.30pm and you can follow all the live action from that match right here.

Chelsea 4 Brighton 3 Leeds 1 Brentford 1 Sunderland 1 Fulham 0.

Possession: Chelsea 26%-74% BrightonShots: 17-15Shots on target: 6-6Corners: 4-7Touches in opposition box: 29-28.

It has been revealed that there is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the new Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

It could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. De Cuyper’s inswinger is clipped into a dangerous area but for some odd reason referee Michael Oliver gives Chelsea a free-kick. Absolutely ridiculous decision; there was no foul in any way, shape or form.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea look to counter through Pedro, who is then brought down by Costinha. It is an easy booking for referee Michael Oliver to give.

According to recent reports, how many added minutes will there be? The answer is five minutes.

Boscagli is booked for bringing down Rogers.

Recent findings suggest that this is a concern for Chelsea as Caicedo, who came on as a second-half substitute, is now having to go off injured. In his place is former Brighton man Barco, who slapped Bellingham at the World Cup. Barco is booed vociferously by the travelling Brighton fans.

Meanwhile Leeds are level 1-1 against Brentford at Elland Road thanks to Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser.

Double change for Brighton as Costinha and David replace Wieffer and Kostoulas.

Brighton scored four a week ago against Aston Villa on the opening weekend but have conceded four this weekend. If they can get a goal though soon, it would make the home fans inside Stamford Bridge very nervous.

Kadioglu has an effort from the edge of the Chelsea box but drags his effort wide.

Meanwhile, up in the north east, Isidor has put Sunderland 1-0 up against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.

Sources indicate that palmer has been pretty quiet today but Chelsea’s two-goal lead is restored. He receives it from Pedro and drives forward through the Brighton half. As he approaches the edge of the penalty area, Palmer calmly slots home into the bottom corner.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Tuchel will have like that. He may not have had a brilliant game, but Palmer just scored a brilliant goal. That should be enough for Chelsea.

Fabian Hurzeler turns to his bench for the first time today as Osman comes on for Yalcouye, who was impressive.

Xabi Alonso turns to his bench again as Chavarria replaces Colwill.

We have this news from the Premier League:.

It has been revealed that #CHEBHAMatch Officials are operating in the second half without communications packs due to an ongoing technical glitch. VAR remains in operation via a back-up system using messages sent to the referee's watch and radio communication to the fourth official if required.

According to recent reports, dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

It has been revealed that chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Recent findings suggest that xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

This game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a substantial deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

According to recent reports, gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

Sources indicate that england head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

According to recent reports, chelsea have two significant chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

It has been revealed that we are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea 3 Brighton 1Leeds 0 Brentford 1Sunderland 0 Fulham 0.

Possession: Chelsea 29%-71% BrightonShots: 9-6Shots on target: 4-3Corners: 2-4Touches in opposition box: 15-10.

In a recent development, chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The first half is then brought to an end not long after and Chelsea take a 3-1 lead into the break.

The Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

In a recent development, there has been a goal in one of the other 2pm kick-offs. At Elland Road, Brentford, who were one of the most impressive teams on the opening weekend, have taken the lead over Leeds through Schade.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

At 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

In a recent development, the Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

The Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. How has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their new goalkeeper.

Industry observers note that brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

The hosts have their second inside the opening quarter of an hour. Rogers does well on the left side of the box to hold off Vuskovic before squaring the ball. Neto runs across Kadioglu’s blindside and pokes home first time from eight yards out. Kadioglu should really have dealt with that and was too flat-footed. Brighton win their first corner of the afternoon and Martinez is forced into action, punching away at his near post as the delivery threatened to creep in.

Chelsea win the first corner of the afternoon after Dunk blocked Neto’s cross...

It has been revealed that xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso noted. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”.

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

It has been revealed that “When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

Recent findings suggest that “We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”.

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

Cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is presently playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

It has been revealed that his son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.
