📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

En conférence de presse hier Ian Cathro, après avoir réfuté toute difficulté de son groupe à performer à l’extérieur, s’est longuement exprimé sur sa gestion de l’effectif, afin de maintenir tout le monde à disposition et est revenu plus précisément sur le cas de son métronome hongrois, Aron Csongvai :.

« On se prépare pour un gros match, un match contre un adversaire très fort. Un match qu’on aborde avec beaucoup de motivation, beaucoup d’ambition. Je ne sais pas si le match sera spectaculaire. Je m’en fiche. Gagner me suffit. On aime tous le foot aussi, et c’est beau quand il y a des bons joueurs sur le terrain. Ça sera un gros match, et on est excité à l’idée de jouer un gros match de foot.

According to recent reports, nos difficultés rencontrées parfois à l’extérieur ne sont pas liées à une question d’être à domicile ou à l’extérieur, mais simplement à la façon dont l’adversaire a  su jouer. C’était le cas à Dijon, même si on a gagné, à Dunkerque même si il était très étrange de perdre ce match . Mais les difficultés venaient plus de la façon dont l’adversaire a su nous déséquilibrer que du fait de jouer à l’extérieur. Peut-être que le seul match où le fait de ne pas jouer à domicile a eu un impact était la fin de match à Metz, parce que là l’ambiance a pu jouer.

Recent findings suggest that contre Rumilly, j’ai préféré notre seconde période à la première. On avait 10 joueurs absents. C’était difficile d’avoir une équipe avec du rythme car les joueurs avaient eu très peu de temps pour trouver des automatismes, peut-être deux entraînements ensemble. La défense a trois a été une option. Je suis très à l’aise avec la défense à trois qui peut être une option bien utile. La seule chose à laquelle je suis marié c’est ma femme. Mon job est d’aider les joueurs à gagner. Une saison de foot est longue. Et ça se joue aussi en fonction des joueurs disponibles. On manage beaucoup le temps de jeu des joueurs pour éviter les problèmes. Donc on doit toujours avoir une option alternative.

Industry observers note that parfois connaître la personne aide à mieux connaître le footballeur. Aron Csongvai fait de l’excellent boulot, il s’est adapté très vite. C’est un mec mature. Il est à une étape de sa vie où il était parfaitement prêt à franchir cette étape, changer de vie, venir dans un plus grand club. N’oublions pas que sa saison a démarré en janvier, ce n’est pas facile. Mais oui il fait vraiment un boulot très notable pour l’équipe. Son rôle c’est de garder l’équilibre avec ou sans le ballon. Il a une grosse responsabilité dans le fait que l’équipe reste équilibrée. L’objectif est de le garder en forme sur les 2 ou 3 mois à venir car je le répète il vient d’une compétition qui a démarré en janvier. Quand les autres clôtureront une saison complète, lui il bouclera une saison ½ de compétition. Donc ce que j’attends de lui c’est qu’il parvienne à rester en forme parce qu’il joue un rôle important dans notre organisation. Donc gardons le en bonne santé et essayons quand c’est possible de lui permettre de se reposer un peu.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, this was the definition of a hard-earned point.
  • Sources indicate that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
  • It has been revealed that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, this was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Sources indicate that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

It has been revealed that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It indicates where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads highlighted major character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

Recent findings suggest that A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

Industry observers note that in truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

According to recent reports, when Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

According to recent reports, the hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under fresh head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. Upcoming signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Sources indicate that marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Invité dans le podcast Kampo animé par le journaliste Smaïl Bouabdellah, Thierry Henry s'est longuement livré sur les coulisses des Jeux Olympiques de Paris 2024.
  • It has been revealed that en 2024 la confection de la liste pour les Jeux Olympiques de Paris avait rapidement viré au casse-tête pour le sélectionneur tricolore.
  • L'attaquant a fait le forcing pour s'assurer une place dans le groupe olympique.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Invité dans le podcast Kampo animé par le journaliste Smaïl Bouabdellah, Thierry Henry s'est longuement livré sur les coulisses des Jeux Olympiques de Paris 2024. L'ancien sélectionneur de l'équipe de France olympique a révélé la détermination totale de Michael Olise pour disputer le tournoi sous le maillot tricolore.

It has been revealed that en 2024 la confection de la liste pour les Jeux Olympiques de Paris avait rapidement viré au casse-tête pour le sélectionneur tricolore. Le tournoi olympique de football n'étant pas inscrit sur les dates officielles du calendrier de la FIFA, les clubs professionnels n'avaient aucune obligation légale de libérer leurs joueurs. Cette absence de contrainte réglementaire avait grandement compliqué la tâche de Thierry Henry pour composer son groupe. Face à ces nombreux refus, Michael Olise a adopté une démarche diamétralement opposée.

L'attaquant a fait le forcing pour s'assurer une place dans le groupe olympique. Alors que Gareth Southgate souhaitait le convoquer avec les A de l'équipe d'Angleterre pour disputer l'Euro 2024, Michael Olise a écarté cette opportunité pour privilégier le maillot tricolore. Le joueur a ainsi multiplié les appels téléphoniques directs avec le sélectionneur français. Dans le podcast Kampo animé par Smaïl Bouabdellah, Thierry Henry a détaillé cette insistance quotidienne : « Michael, il m’appelait tous les jours pour aller aux JO, alors qu’il y avait l’équipe d’Angleterre qui le voulait pour aller au Championnat d’Europe avec les A. Il aurait pu aller à l’Euro avec l’Angleterre. Mais il m’appelait tous les jours. Son envie de jouer pour l’équipe de France était extraordinaire. Moi, je n’ai convaincu personne. ».

Né à Londres en 2001 d'un père nigérian et d'une mère franco-algérienne, Michael Olise disposait sur le proposal sportif de plusieurs options internationales. L'attaquant était éligible pour quatre sélections nationales différentes : la France, l'Angleterre, le Nigeria et l'Algérie. Toutefois, Michael Olise a toujours accordé sa préférence absolue à l'équipe de France. Au-delà des approches anglaises, le joueur a fait preuve d'une fermeté totale au moment de quitter Crystal Palace pour rejoindre l'Allemagne.

In a recent development, recruté par le Bayern Munich pour 53 millions d'euros selon Foot Mercato, et plus de 60 millions d'euros d'après d'autres sources, il a imposé sa participation aux Jeux Olympiques de Paris 2024. Le joueur a ainsi pris le risque de se heurter à sa nouvelle direction bavaroise pour défendre les couleurs tricolores. Thierry Henry a salué cette prise de position au micro de Smaïl Bouabdellah : « Michael Olise aime l’équipe de France depuis qu’il est petit. Certains joueurs ne voulaient pas venir. Pas de problème, je n’en veux à personne. Mais un mec de ce calibre est venu, alors qu’il y avait le risque de s’embrouiller avec son nouveau club. Il m’a dit: 'Où je vais, je vais dire à mon club que je vais aux Jeux olympiques, c’est tout.’ On parle de Michael Olise. Mon respect pour lui est énorme. ».

Sur le terrain, ce choix a porté ses fruits tout au long de la compétition estivale. Titulaire lors des 6 matches du tournoi olympique, Michael Olise a compilé 2 buts et 5 passes décisives sous les ordres de Thierry Henry. Ce parcours s'est achevé par une médaille d'argent décrochée le 9 août 2024 au Parc des Princes, après une finale disputée contre l'Espagne (3-5 après prolongation).

According to recent reports, au-delà de ce bilan chiffré, Thierry Henry qualifie Michael Olise de génie qu'il ne faut pas brider. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bousculée et imprécise lors du premier acte dimanche soir, l'équipe de France a affiché un tout autre visage après la pause face à la Turquie. Un sursaut salutaire provoqué par Zinédine Zidane, qui n'a pas hésité à hausser le ton dans le vestiaire.

According to recent reports, dimanche 15 novembre, les Bleus disputaient la 6e et dernière journée de la Ligue des nations face à la Turquie au stade Atlantique de Bordeaux. Trois jours après le revers concédé face à l'Italie à San Siro, premier accroc de l'ère Zinédine Zidane, les Tricolores se devaient de réagir. Toutefois, à la pause, le score restait nul et vierge (0-0), actant un dixième match de suite sans marquer lors du premier acte. Un manque d'efficacité chronique qui a fini par agacer le sélectionneur.

It has been revealed that dans le vestiaire tricolore, Zinédine Zidane a recadré ses joueurs, sans pour autant céder à une colère excessive. Le sélectionneur souhaitait corriger l'apathie collective et le manque d'agressivité à la perte du ballon constatés durant le premier acte. Une mise au point nécessaire pour relancer son équipe. Au micro de TF1 après la rencontre, le défenseur de Liverpool Jérémy Jacquet a ainsi dévoilé la teneur du discours : « Le coach nous a dit à la mi-temps qu’il trouvait qu’on n’était pas assez agressifs à la perte du ballon. On l’a bien rectifié en deuxième. […] Pour être honnête, il n’a pas gueulé, mais a haussé le ton sur nos axes de progression à la perte de balle. Pour lui, on pouvait faire mieux. Il trouvait qu’on gardait trop le ballon et voulait que l’on bouge plus. ».

De son côté, le technicien tricolore a confirmé avoir bousculé ses troupes tout en restant mesuré, préférant insister sur les ajustements tactiques exigés sur la pelouse. « Ce n'est pas la défense. C'est tous ensemble. On doit aller presser tous ensemble et quand on ne presse pas, on se resserre tous ensemble. C'est des choses qu'on doit mettre en place. On a besoin de garder le ballon. On aime courir avec ballon, sans ballon, ce n'est pas notre truc. On l'a mieux en seconde période en jouant en deux touches. On doit le répéter. Les murs n’ont pas tremblé à la mi-temps. On a rectifié des choses et c’était mieux en seconde. La réaction était très bonne », a détaillé Zinédine Zidane sur TF1.

En effet, la copie rendue au cours des quarante-cinq premières minutes a déçu le patron des Bleus. Malgré une possession de balle établie à 60 %, la France n'a jamais su emballer la rencontre, gaspillant de l'énergie à courir après le cuir tout en concédant de larges décalages. Le pressing tricolore s'est révélé particulièrement inefficace. Sur le plateau de TF1, Zinédine Zidane a ainsi exprimé sa frustration : « C'était l'objectif de se qualifier, en étant éventuellement premier. Par contre, sur le contenu, on peut être un peu perplexe, surtout dans notre pression en première mi-temps. Quand on ne voit pas certaines choses sur le terrain, on est un peu frustrés. C'est surtout dans la pression, parce qu'on laissait faire les décalages et on n'a pas été bons du tout dans notre pression. On a rectifié ça à la mi-temps et on a été meilleurs après. Ce sont des choses où on doit encore s'améliorer. Moi, je n'étais pas content, les joueurs non plus. Mais on a rectifié. ».

D'ailleurs, le sélectionneur a réitéré son agacement en conférence de presse d'après-match pour cibler ce dysfonctionnement inhabituel. Pour Zinédine Zidane, son équipe a été défaillante dans sa première ligne de récupération en concédant bien trop de liberté à l'adversaire : « Ce qui n’a pas été bon, c’est notre première pression. On l’a très bien fait sur les cinq autres matchs, même contre l’Italie. En revanche, ce soir, on a été défaillants, notamment en première mi-temps. On a laissé beaucoup trop d’espaces. On a rectifié le tir en deuxième mi-temps où on a été très bons dans l’utilisation du ballon. Même si on peut encore mieux faire, parce que j’ai des joueurs de qualité qui peuvent garder le ballon. Ce sont eux (les Turcs) qui doivent courir derrière le ballon », a insisté Zinédine Zidane.

It has been revealed that au retour des vestiaires, le discours du sélectionneur a porté ses fruits. Nettement plus agressifs et tranchants en jouant en deux touches de balle, les Bleus ont rapidement trouvé la faille sur un but contre son camp d'Emirhan Topçu (49e). Lancés, les Tricolores ont ensuite fait le break grâce à Éli Junior Kroupi (79e). La réduction du score tardive d'Abdülkerim Bardakcı (89e) n'a rien changé à l'issue de la rencontre (2-1). Une réaction salutaire.

According to recent reports, ainsi, ce succès combiné à la défaite de l'Italie contre la Belgique (1-4) permet à la France de terminer à la première place de sa poule. Les hommes de Zinédine Zidane valident officiellement leur qualification pour les quarts de finale du Final 8 de la Ligue des nations. Les Bleus connaîtront leur prochain adversaire lors du tirage au sort programmé le vendredi 20 novembre 2026 en Suisse, avant d'aborder cette double confrontation en mars 2027.

En raison des départs précipités des joueurs, le sélectionneur de l'équipe de France a dû faire l'impasse sur son discours d'après-match.

According to recent reports, dimanche 15 novembre 2026, l'équipe de France a conclu sa phase de groupes de Ligue des nations par un succès contre la Turquie (2-1), devant 42 000 spectateurs au stade Atlantique de Bordeaux. Lors de cette 6e et dernière journée, les Bleus ont marqué un premier but grâce à une réalisation contre son camp d'Emirhan Topçu à la 49e minute, puis un deuxième avec Éli Junior Kroupi à la 80e minute, avant la réduction du score turque par Abdülkerim Bardakcı à la 90e minute. Le coup de sifflet final a retenti à 22h38. Une fin de soirée agitée.

À 22h40, les Bleus ont effectué un timide tour d'honneur autour du rond central plutôt qu'autour du terrain, sans plusieurs cadres dont le capitaine Kylian Mbappé qui avait déjà quitté la pelouse. D'ailleurs, la distance entre les joueurs et les tribunes lors de ce tour d'honneur a provoqué quelques sifflets de supporters français déçus.

Sources indicate that en effet, les départs se sont enchaînés à toute vitesse. Kylian Mbappé a quitté le stade Atlantique à 22h53, soit exactement quinze minutes après le coup de sifflet final, plusieurs témoins évoquant un joueur très pressé. Rayan Cherki et Malo Gusto ont ensuite quitté le stade ensemble valise à la main, suivis par Eduardo Camavinga. Une course contre la montre.

Et pour cause, la fermeture avancée de l'aéroport de Bordeaux-Mérignac imposait un timing très serré. Plusieurs avions privés étaient ainsi prévus au décollage : un jet pour Milan à 00h05 et un autre pour Madrid à 00h12. De son côté, l'avion de la Fédération Française de Football a quitté la Gironde à 1h15.

Passés en zone d'interviews, Andy Diouf et Pablo Pagis ont tous les deux confirmé l'absence de discours de Zinédine Zidane dans le vestiaire. « On n’a pas fait de discours », a déclaré Andy Diouf devant les micros. De son côté, Pablo Pagis a détaillé la gestion du sélectionneur tricolore : « Il a laissé tout le monde tranquille ».

Zinédine Zidane n'a pas retenu ses joueurs pressés en raison de la fatigue et du calendrier très serré de ce rassemblement de novembre, qui comptait deux matches en 72 heures.

In a recent development, au-delà de cette fin de soirée au pas de course dans les couloirs du stade bordelais, les Tricolores ont validé leur qualification. Le prochain rendez-vous des Bleus de Zidane est fixé du 25 au 30 mars 2027 pour les quarts de finale aller-retour de la Ligue des nations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ciblé par de vives critiques après la récente défaite du Brésil, Carlo Ancelotti a réagi ce lundi avec une fermeté inhabituelle. Le sélectionneur de la Seleção a sèchement répondu aux attaques de Romario, qui réclamait publiquement son départ immédiat.

La tension est montée d'un cran autour de la sélection brésilienne depuis le revers concédé face au Japon (3-2), samedi 14 novembre 2026, au Stade national de Singapour. Alors que les Japonais menaient rapidement grâce à Takefusa Kubo et Keito Nakamura, le doublé de Vinícius Júnior (33e, 75e) avait pourtant permis aux Auriverdes d'égaliser. Toutefois, le but concédé à Tatsuhiro Sakamoto (91e) dans le temps additionnel a scellé la défaite brésilienne.

Présent en conférence de presse d'avant-match à Singapour, Carlo Ancelotti a été invité à réagir aux attaques formulées par l'ancien attaquant de la Seleção. Le technicien italien a répondu en espagnol à l'ancien international. Une mise au point limpide. « C'est la liberté d'expression et, dans un pays démocratique, tout le monde peut avoir une opinion. Romario a donné la sienne, et tout le monde a le droit de dire des mensonges, des vérités ou des bêtises. Ce qui est sûr, c'est que Romario parle beaucoup, et il est dans son droit », a ainsi rétorqué l'entraîneur face aux journalistes.

Sources indicate that cette sortie directe démontre la volonté du sélectionneur de balayer la polémique alors que la pression médiatique s'accentue. Carlo Ancelotti n'a pas souhaité polémiquer davantage avec l'ancienne gloire du football brésilien, se contentant de souligner avec ironie l'omniprésence médiatique de son détracteur.

Recent findings suggest that deux jours plus tôt, Romario n'avait pas mâché ses mots à la suite de la défaite concédée face à l'équipe nippone. L'ancien buteur brésilien avait réclamé la destitution immédiate du sélectionneur sur ses réseaux sociaux, estimant qu'Ancelotti ne disposait pas des qualités requises pour diriger le pays. « Ça suffit ! Prends tes affaires et va-t'en ! », avait notamment écrit Romario, très remonté contre l'entraîneur italien.

According to recent reports, au-delà de cette interpellation, Romario a tout de même reconnu les accomplissements passés de Carlo Ancelotti, qualifié d'« un des grands entraîneurs » en club, tout en appelant à son retour sur le Vieux Continent : « Retourne dans les clubs, où tu t'es fait un nom, car la sélection brésilienne ne peut pas continuer à prendre ce risque ». L'ancien international a également interpellé le président de la Confédération brésilienne de football (CBF), Samir Xaud, affirmant qu'il fallait désormais « le courage de prendre une décision ». Cette attaque fait suite à une fin de match sous haute tension contre le Japon, au cours de laquelle Carlo Ancelotti et l'attaquant Raphinha avaient été expulsés pour avoir protesté contre une faute présumée au départ de la troisième réalisation adverse.

Lucide quant au niveau affiché par ses joueurs sur le terrain, Carlo Ancelotti n'a éludé aucune question sur les difficultés actuelles de la Seleção. Lors de son point presse, le coach italien a dressé une autocritique sans concession sur le rendement de son groupe. « Je dois faire plus et je vais le faire. J'aime être ici, j'aime être dans la sélection nationale et je dois m'améliorer. Je dois faire plus pour que la sélection redevienne compétitive. Il y a longtemps que nous ne sommes plus compétitifs », a déclaré le technicien italien.

Toutefois, le sélectionneur brésilien a insisté sur la nature amicale de cette rencontre et la nécessité de renouveler son effectif en vue des futures échéances. « C'est évident que c'est le moment des essais. Nous essayons de nouveaux joueurs, en commençant par Gabriel Bontempo, André, Jonathan Jesus... Ce sont des évaluations très positives, sans mentionner de noms. Nous espérons toujours bien jouer, mais il est incompatible d'essayer, de renouveler et d'avoir l'équipe prête. Nous continuons avec une grande confiance dans cette voie et nous nous testerons contre Singapour », a détaillé le sélectionneur brésilien.

Après ce premier revers en Asie, le Brésil doit désormais se remobiliser pour son second match amical de la trêve internationale, prévu le mardi 17 novembre 2026 au Stade national de Singapour face à Singapour. Une rencontre que Carlo Ancelotti devra observer loin de la pelouse : le technicien italien est suspendu de banc de touche suite à son expulsion contre le Japon et ne pourra pas diriger directement ses hommes au bord du terrain. L'équipe devra également composer sans son attaquant Raphinha, lui aussi sous le coup d'une suspension. Pour animer son secteur offensif face aux Singapouriens, Carlo Ancelotti a d'ores et déjà annoncé la titularisation du jeune avant-centre Endrick pour le match du mardi 17 novembre 2026.

C'est une annonce majeure pour le football belge en ce lundi 16 novembre 2026. Sur son compte Instagram, Romelu Lukaku a officialisé son départ définitif de la sélection des Diables Rouges après seize années passées au plus haut niveau international.

According to recent reports, L'attaquant de 33 ans a surpris l'ensemble des observateurs au lendemain de la victoire de la Belgique face à l'Italie (4-1) en Ligue des nations, qui a validé la qualification des Diables Rouges pour les quarts de finale du tournoi. Dimanche 15 novembre 2026, Romelu Lukaku est resté sur le banc des remplaçants sans entrer en jeu, après avoir manqué le match précédent face à la Turquie en raison d'une légère blessure à la hanche. Pour accompagner son message d'adieu sur le réseau social, le joueur a publié une galerie photo retraçant son parcours international depuis ses débuts en mars 2010 à l'âge de 16 ans. Plusieurs coéquipiers emblématiques de la génération dorée, dont Axel Witsel et Thibaut Courtois, ont d'ailleurs salué publiquement sa carrière sous sa publication. Une page se tourne pour les Diables Rouges.

Sources indicate that en quittant la sélection, Romelu Lukaku laisse un héritage statistique considérable. L'avant-centre se retire en effet en tant que meilleur buteur absolu de l'histoire de la sélection belge avec 94 buts inscrits en 135 sélections. Au niveau des apparitions, le joueur n'est devancé que par Jan Vertonghen (157 sélections) et Axel Witsel (140 sélections). Pilier de la sélection durant plus d'une décennie, il a disputé quatre phases finales de Coupe du monde (2014, 2018 avec une 3e place, 2022 et 2026) ainsi que trois Championnats d'Europe (2016, 2020 et 2024). Son dernier match officiel sous le maillot des Diables Rouges remonte ainsi au 5 octobre 2026 contre l'équipe de France en Ligue des nations, lors d'une défaite (1-4).

Recent findings suggest that cette annonce constitue d'ailleurs un revirement par rapport aux plans initialement affichés par l'intéressé. En effet, l'attaquant avait affirmé en janvier 2026 que la Coupe du monde 2026 ne marquerait pas sa dernière compétition majeure avec la Belgique. La sélection des Diables Rouges a elle aussi tenu à rendre hommage à son avant-centre sur son compte officiel X, saluant un joueur qui a écrit un incroyable chapitre de l'histoire de l'équipe nationale.

La situation sportive de l'attaquant s'était toutefois compliquée lors des dernières semaines avec les Diables Rouges. Depuis la prise de fonction de Mark van Bommel comme sélectionneur en août 2026 en remplacement de Rudi Garcia, Romelu Lukaku a vu son temps de jeu diminuer au profit de Charles De Ketelaere. Resté sur le banc lors du récent succès face à l'Italie, le joueur a finalement choisi de renoncer aux prochaines échéances internationales de son pays. En effet, la Belgique disputera les quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations du 25 au 30 mars 2027, dont le tirage au sort est fixé au vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à Nyon.

Industry observers note that toutefois, cette retraite internationale ne met absolument pas un terme à sa carrière en club. Romelu Lukaku évolue sous les couleurs de Fenerbahçe depuis le mois d'août 2026 et reste concentré sur ses objectifs en Turquie. L'attaquant disputera ainsi son prochain match officiel le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 17h00 face à Kocaelispor en Süper Lig.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Présent en conférence de presse ce lundi 16 novembre 2026 à Singapour, Vinicius Jr a livré une mise au point sans détour sur ses récentes difficultés avec le Real Madrid. L'attaquant brésilien a admis avoir diminué son volume d'entraînement estival, profondément affecté par l'élimination précoce de sa sélection lors de la dernière Coupe du monde.

Ce début d'exercice s'avère particulièrement difficile pour le joueur de 26 ans sous les couleurs du club espagnol. Avec un bilan de seulement un but et trois passes décisives en 12 rencontres toutes compétitions confondues avec le Real Madrid, Vinicius Jr traverse une période délicate. Un rendement bien loin de ses standards. La cause de ce passage à vide trouve son origine dans les suites de la Coupe du monde, où le Brésil a quitté la compétition dès les huitièmes de finale après une défaite face à la Norvège (2-1). Très affecté par ce revers, l'attaquant a ainsi privilégié le repos et la déconnexion en famille durant ses vacances, au détriment de sa préparation physique.

Devant les médias à Singapour, l'ailier madrilène a d'ailleurs détaillé avec franchise les raisons de ce déficit athlétique :.

Au-delà de cette déception internationale, le contexte extra-sportif n'a pas aidé le joueur du Real Madrid à aborder cette saison l'esprit totalement libéré. En effet, le dossier de sa prolongation contractuelle et les sollicitations extérieures, notamment l'intérêt de clubs comme Arsenal, ont perturbé sa concentration estivale. L'attaquant a ainsi reconnu que ces remous avaient directement influé sur son niveau de jeu depuis la reprise.

Toutefois, l'ailier madrilène a tenu à rappeler la difficulté de se maintenir au sommet dans la durée. Pour appuyer son constat, il a souligné que seuls Cristiano Ronaldo et Lionel Messi ont su afficher de telles statistiques pendant de longues années. Le numéro 7 brésilien a également rappelé son devoir d'exemplarité, affirmant être conscient que s'il court davantage, tous les jeunes joueurs courront aussi plus.

Recent findings suggest that vinicius Jr a tempéré les inquiétudes en comparant sa trajectoire à celle de la saison passée, où il ne comptait que 5 buts en décembre avant de dépasser la barre des 20 réalisations au printemps. L'attaquant reste ainsi convaincu que sa montée en puissance physique portera ses fruits au moment opportun.

Sur le proposal sportif en sélection, Vinicius Jr s'est d'ailleurs redonné de la confiance en signant un doublé samedi 14 novembre 2026 lors de la défaite du Brésil contre le Japon (2-3) au Stade national de Singapour. Le Brésil dispute désormais son prochain match amical face à Singapour le mardi 17 novembre 2026 à 11h00 (heure française) au Stade national de Singapour. Le prochain rendez-vous de Vinicius Jr avec le Real Madrid est ensuite programmé le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 21h00 face au Celta Vigo au stade Santiago-Bernabéu pour la 13e journée de Liga.

L’ex giocatore biancoceleste e del Milan ha parlato del rapporto con l’amico ed ex compagno di squadra in un’intervista a Repubblica. Oltre al giudizio sull’attuale allenatore della Lazio, ha ricordato il ruolo che aveva nello spogliatoio rossonero e alcuni episodi vissuti insieme.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, secondo Oddo, l’esperienza da commissario tecnico della Nazionale, conclusa senza la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha inciso sulla consapevolezza di Gattuso. Da ct, mancando la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha subito una delle lezioni sportive più grandi della sua carriera, non solo per il risultato. Adesso ha preso ancora più consapevolezza di prima».

Industry observers note that oddo riconosce nell’allenatore della Lazio un ruolo che aveva già ai tempi del Milan: «ma è sempre stato un “braccio armato” pronto a intervenire e risolvere i momenti di crisi. Già ai tempi del Milan. Rino rieducava senza mai punire». Il richiamo arrivava anche per piccoli ritardi e, nel suo racconto, non richiedeva l’intervento del club.

L’ex compagno precisa: «bastavano due minuti di ritardo – capitava soprattutto ai brasiliani, esclusi Dida e Kakà – e scattava il rimprovero. Non serviva l’intervento della società».

Industry News: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?
  • Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.
  • Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

According to recent reports, the big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams remarked: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

Recent findings suggest that glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” noted Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

It has been revealed that “The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

According to recent reports, while Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

In a recent development, one of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi remarked: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

Sources indicate that “If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with substantial qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi noted: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1.

Pierre Sage has his first win while Alvaro Arbeloa has lost his first three Premier League games and go to Anfield next Saturday. Frank de Boer vibes.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

In a recent development, brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘fresh’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

Iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

In a recent development, enzo jeered by Coventry fans when taken off was predictable. Replaced by Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Jaidon Anthony bundled the ball in but had used his hands.

And Mykhailo Mudryk is on for his first appearance since November 2024.

The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca noted, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more key to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

Sources indicate that “Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just mentioned he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

Sources indicate that “I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”.

Sources indicate that maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi aims to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Industry observers note that palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

It has been revealed that bayern Munich’s Harry Kane became the first Bundesliga player to win the Ballon d’Or in 30 years, lifting the prestigious trophy ahead of Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal. Speaking exclusively to t-online, Bayern president Herbert Hainer discussed the significance of Kane claiming the coveted prize, awarded to the world’s best footballer, for both him and Germany’s record champions.

Industry observers note that “The significance of this cannot be overstated, both for Harry Kane and for Bayern and the entire Bundesliga,” explained Hainer. “We have the World Player of the Year in Germany, that’s an international exclamation mark. On Bayern’s club media channels, we shattered all previous records in terms of reach that day.

It has been revealed that “Harry has developed even further here. For him, it wasn’t just an award for one season, but for his achievements over the past few years – as a footballer and as a person. He’s a role model off the pitch as well. Furthermore, he’s shown that at Bayern, you can achieve anything individually.”.

Kane returned 73 games across all competitions for both Bayern and England last season, and he’s already in unstoppable form this term, plundering 10 goals and providing a further 10 assists in 15 appearances across all competitions for die Rekordmeister.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, bayern Munich legend and honorary president Uli Hoeneß believes Jürgen Klopp can restore the discipline and hunger he feels have been missing from the German national team. Speaking at the Sport BILD Awards, Hoeneß backed the Germany head coach to impose his personality on the team while stressing that the rebuilding process will require patience.

“I think he will bring discipline and hunger back in,” Hoeneß stated. “He is hungry himself. But I didn’t expect him to lay hands on everything to move promptly. We need to give him time. I also expect that many things will improve under Per Mertesacker, who is now overseeing the youth setup.”.

Klopp’s Germany delivered their clearest statement yet on Monday night, thrashing the Netherlands 5-0 at Berlin’s Olympiastadion. The emphatic victory secured top spot in Nations League Group A2 and a place in the quarter-finals, giving Germany a significant result as Klopp continues to reshape the national team.

Recent findings suggest that hoeneß’s comments on hunger were not restricted to Klopp or the German national team. The 74-year-old argued that German football has been affected by broader social changes, recalling the environment in which he developed as a young player.

“I used to play football on the street after school, from two in the afternoon until nightfall,” Hoeneß noted. “That no longer exists today. We live in a country where most people are doing very well. I see this as the greatest danger for our football as well. If someone comes from Brazil, Portugal, or Argentina, they want to climb the social ladder. That is what we lack.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We must learn again to work hard if we want to be successful,” Hoeneß continued. “That applies not only to footballers, but to the whole country.”.

For Hoeneß, Klopp’s task therefore extends beyond tactical adjustments or short-term results. The Bayern honorary president believes restoring the mentality he associates with successful German teams will be just as key as the structural work being undertaken in Germany’s youth setup.

In a recent development, rising Borussia Mönchengladbach star Wael Mohya (17) – who has scored two goals and provided one assist in nine Bundesliga games in 2026/27, and earned a call-up to Jürgen Klopp’s Germany squad – has featured in every league match for the Foals this season, launching himself into the limelight after making his top flight debut in December 2025. Now, the 17-year-old is attracting interest from Europe’s biggest clubs.

According to Sport Bild, Bayer Leverkusen are planning to meet with Mohya’s entourage with discussions with the player, his family, and Gladbach to follow. In addition to Leverkusen, Liverpool Bayern Munich, RB Leipzig and Brighton and Hove Albion are all interested in signing the youngster.

Mohya’s current deal expires in 2028 and while Gladbach want to extend the player’s contract beyond that, failure to reach an agreement could force their hand as they don’t want to lose the player for free in 2028. As such, a transfer fee in the region of €20m may be enough to entice Borussia, should they not be able to persuade the young attacker to extend his contract.

#2901. Industry News: FEATURE | Six winners from the Germany U21 November 2026 international break

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Getfootballnewsgermany ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: FEATURE | Six winners from the Germany U21 November 2026 international break

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3832 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that antonio Di Salvo’s Germany U21s managed to conclude their 2026 calendar year with two consecutive friendly defeats during the November international break, falling 2-1 to Belgium in Essen before surrendering a second-half lead in a bizarre 3-2 loss to Croatia in Rijeka.
  • While such results certainly weren’t what Di Salvo and his staff had envisioned, the fact that neither result carried competitive consequences should temper the disappointment.
  • The Belgium encounter featured some encouraging attacking football, particularly from players who had only recently entered or returned to the U21 setup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that antonio Di Salvo’s Germany U21s managed to conclude their 2026 calendar year with two consecutive friendly defeats during the November international break, falling 2-1 to Belgium in Essen before surrendering a second-half lead in a bizarre 3-2 loss to Croatia in Rijeka. The results brought an abrupt end to an impressive eight-match winning streak and left the DFB youngsters with plenty to contemplate ahead of next summer’s UEFA European U21 Championship.

While such results certainly weren’t what Di Salvo and his staff had envisioned, the fact that neither result carried competitive consequences should temper the disappointment. Moreover, the international break wasn’t nearly as disappointing as the scorelines suggested. Our Get German Football News analysis of two matches yields just one fewer ‘winner’ than our long-form check on Jürgen Klopp’s senior men’s team.

The Belgium encounter featured some encouraging attacking football, particularly from players who had only recently entered or returned to the U21 setup. The Germans repeatedly created dangerous situations through aggressive pressing, midfield combinations, and individual attacking initiative. Unfortunately, defensive lapses and insufficient precision in front of goal undermined much of the positive work.

Tuesday’s fixture against Croatia proved an entirely different proposition. Torrential rainfall, thick fog, and a playing surface that gradually transformed into something resembling a collection of small lakes made meaningful football almost impossible. Di Salvo’s team nevertheless recovered from a 1-0 halftime deficit to take the lead before the hosts scored twice in the final 25 minutes.

Industry observers note that the conditions prompted the German U21 coach to question whether anything meaningful could be learned from the encounter. Speaking at the post-match press conference attended by Get German Football News, Di Salvo expressed relief that the players had escaped injury and emphasized that the earlier Belgium match offered a more useful opportunity for analysis.

There is another crucial consideration.

In a recent development, the November squad had been weakened considerably by injuries and withdrawals. Established U21 contributors such as Tom Bischof, Lennart Karl, and Remarked El Mala were also unavailable because of their involvement with Jürgen Klopp’s senior national team. The absence of captain Nicolo Tresoldi, who suffered a concussion in training, required Di Salvo to make significant alterations to his attacking intends.

The personnel difficulties opened opportunities for several players attempting to establish themselves at Germany’s highest youth level.

Some seized their chances rather emphatically.

In a recent development, the author is thus pleased to present six winners from the November international break. The selections take account of individual performances, tactical contributions, and the extent to which players improved their standing ahead of next summer’s European Championship.

Few players entered November with more to gain than Cajetan Lenz. The 20-year-old made his Germany U21 debut against Belgium after previously earning nine appearances at U20 level and below. His promotion came at a particularly interesting stage in his club career.

Lenz emerged as one of the most impressive young midfielders in the 2. Bundesliga during his breakthrough campaign at Bochum, making 31 league appearances and attracting considerable interest from top-flight clubs. Get German Football News identified the youngster as a potential Bayer Leverkusen transfer target in its December 2025 transfer primer. Eintracht Frankfurt also pursued the midfielder before Hoffenheim ultimately secured his services.

The move has nevertheless presented some unforeseen difficulties.

Industry observers note that as GGFN examined following Lenz’s U21 debut, the midfielder has struggled to break into Christian Ilzer’s Bundesliga team, accumulating just three minutes of league football this season. His performances for Germany therefore carried particular significance. Lenz operated alongside Noël Aseko in central midfield against Belgium, contributing to several encouraging attacking sequences and repeatedly driving forward to support the team’s more advanced players.

His energetic movement was especially key during Germany’s stronger first-half periods, when the hosts attempted to establish control through combinations involving Damar, Brunner, and the left-sided players. The debutant’s willingness to carry possession forward and participate in attacking movements offered an encouraging contrast to his limited opportunities at club level.

Industry observers note that di Salvo was clearly impressed. Speaking at the post-match press conference in Essen, the coach specifically identified Lenz as one of the players who had made a positive impression upon the coaching staff.

It has been revealed that “It’s a little early to discuss the [2027 UEFA U21] European championship roster,” Di Salvo remarked on Friday. “There are still many games to be played and many lads who, of course, aren’t here. And yet, there are some who – with their performances – have managed to make a mark with their impressions.”.

“Namely, Cajetan Lenz, who played a very good game today,” Di Salvo continued. “He’s had very little playing time and I was thus pleased to see him log 85 minutes today. It was good that he could plow on through. From time to time he lacked clarity and the last pass was somewhat imprecise.

“But in general, he delivered a fantastic performance,” Di Salvo concluded. “He really ran a lot and marched forward. With that, particularly in light of his lack of playing time, we’re really satisfied with him.”.

It has been revealed that lenz followed his impressive debut with another encouraging appearance against Croatia. The Hoffenheim professional remained active despite the deteriorating conditions, nearly breaking into the penalty area early in the second half and heading narrowly wide from a Tom Rothe cross in the 51st minute.

Two minutes later, he provided the decisive touch from Damar’s free kick that enabled Moerstedt to score Germany’s equalizer. The youngster continued his attacking involvement throughout the second half, although he would undoubtedly have preferred a better outcome when Pejcinovic’s 82nd-minute shot rebounded into his path.

His failure to convert that opportunity represented one of Germany’s more frustrating moments during the final stages, but two consecutive 7/10 ratings constitute an impressive return for a player making his first two appearances at this level.

Industry observers note that lenz himself appeared determined to maintain realistic expectations when speaking to GGFN in the mixed zone after the Belgium encounter. The midfielder emphasized his gratitude for the opportunity while acknowledging that he remained a challenger for a regular position.

Di Salvo’s subsequent praise suggests that the youngster has already made considerable progress toward that objective.

In a recent development, brunner’s inclusion hardly requires justification given his consistency across both matches. The former Germany U17 World Champion earned 8/10 ratings from GGFN against both Belgium and Croatia, emerging as one of the few German attackers capable of producing threatening moments throughout the international break.

It has been revealed that brunner’s November responsibilities were considerably different from those he had assumed earlier in the qualification campaign. As GGFN examined in its October Germany U21 Tactics Check, Di Salvo had previously enjoyed considerable success with a versatile attacking trio consisting of Brunner, Tresoldi, and Dzenan Pejcinovic. Tresoldi’s absence forced the coach to reconsider how best to organize his forwards.

Against Belgium, Brunner took on the central attacking assignment while Muhammed Damar moved onto the left. The Monaco professional began energetically and continued to involve himself in Germany’s attacking combinations, even if the hosts frequently lacked precision with their final deliveries.

According to recent reports, one of Brunner’s more vital contributions came in the 24th minute, when he drew the foul that provided Damar with the opportunity to equalize from a free kick. Brunner subsequently participated in the attacking sequence that resulted in Damar’s second effort against the crossbar in the 58th minute.

The youngster continued searching for a goal after Damar’s substitution, attempting an acrobatic finish in the 71st minute and producing several further incursions into the Belgian penalty area. The Croatia match offered an opportunity to demonstrate an additional dimension of his game.

Brunner began alongside Pejcinovic in what appeared to be a narrow 4-2-2-2. At halftime, however, Di Salvo introduced Max Moerstedt and deliberately shifted Brunner onto the left. The adjustment worked exceptionally well. Brunner became one of Germany’s most productive attacking players after the interval. His delivery for Pejcinovic’s 60th-minute goal supplied the visitors with a 2-1 lead, and the Monaco professional also struck the post during Germany’s strongest attacking spell.

Di Salvo deliberately and justifiably singled the 20-year-old out for praise after the break had officially concluded.

It has been revealed that while Brunner stands out for his consistency, Damar can reasonably claim to have delivered the outstanding individual performance of the international break. The Wolfsburg attacker returned to the U21 starting XI against Belgium following an extended absence and promptly produced a display worthy of GGFN’s Player of the Match award and a 9/10 rating.

According to recent reports, it proved quite the joy to observe Damar’s stated determination to make the most of his national-team comeback manifest itself on the pitch. The 22-year-old began the first fixture shot out of a cannon and proceeded to cover nearly every blade of grass on the pitch. Beginning on the left wing, he frequently rotated into central areas and occasionally appeared on the opposite flank, creating considerable difficulty for the Belgian defenders attempting to track him.

His equalizer in the 25th minute was particularly memorable.

It has been revealed that having earned another opportunity from a dead ball, Damar cleverly drove his free kick underneath the jumping Belgian defensive wall. The technique was unusual, the execution excellent, and the subsequent celebration both touching and unforgettable.

Recent findings suggest that he wasn’t finished. A second free kick in the 38th minute was tipped onto the crossbar. He struck the woodwork again in the 58th following an excellent attacking combination with Pejcinovic and Brunner. There were stretches of the match during which Damar appeared determined to generate virtually every meaningful German attacking opportunity himself.

Speaking to GGFN and other journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Damar explained the instinctive decision behind his free-kick goal, expressed frustration about his missed opportunities, and spoke enthusiastically about the pride he takes in representing Germany.

His performance against Croatia was considerably less influential but that had much to do with the fact that the waterlogged surface made life particularly difficult for a technical attacker who relies upon close control, quick changes of direction, and precise passing. Damar nevertheless remained involved in Germany’s attacking moves and supplied the free kick from which Cajetan Lenz helped create Moerstedt’s equalizer.

The author still saw fit to award him a 6/10 in Rijeka.

Overall, Damar’s international comeback constituted an unequivocal success.

What a difference 45 minutes can make. Moerstedt’s November international break began with an unexpected call-up following Nicolo Tresoldi’s injury withdrawal and concluded with his first Germany U21 goal and a GGFN Player of the Match award.

The Hoffenheim striker only joined the squad after the international break had begun, making his U21 debut as an 86th-minute substitute against Belgium. There was little time for him to influence that fixture. GGFN awarded Moerstedt a 5/10, reflecting his brief involvement rather than any particularly poor performance.

Industry observers note that croatia presented a substantially greater opportunity. With Germany trailing 1-0 at halftime, Di Salvo introduced the youngster as part of a four-player substitution package. The coach wanted more presence inside the Croatian penalty area and consequently repositioned Brunner onto the left.

Moerstedt responded almost immediately. Germany emerged with greater attacking purpose, and the Hoffenheim striker began involving himself in combinations with the midfielders and his fellow forwards.

In a recent development, in the 53rd minute, Lenz redirected Damar’s free kick toward Moerstedt inside the Croatian penalty area. The striker’s initial effort was blocked, but he reacted quickly enough to recover possession and convert at the second attempt.

The equalizer changed the direction of the match and helped establish the momentum that eventually produced Germany’s second goal. There was much to admire about Moerstedt’s performance beyond the finish itself.

In a recent development, the 20-year-old offered the type of physical presence and determination inside the box that Germany had lacked during the opening half. He remained available for deliveries despite the increasingly treacherous surface and helped occupy Croatian defenders as Brunner and Pejcinovic enjoyed greater freedom in attack.

Moerstedt’s first goal came in only his second U21 appearance, and his performance in Rijeka earned him an 8/10 rating. With Tresoldi expected to remain an notable figure in Di Salvo’s intends, the competition for the central attacking position will undoubtedly be intense.

Moerstedt has nevertheless made an impressive opening argument for further opportunities.

According to recent reports, the next place goes to a midfielder who quietly delivered two of Germany’s more consistent performances during an otherwise difficult international break. Noël Aseko earned 7/10 ratings against both Belgium and Croatia, providing important energy and physical commitment in central midfield.

Sources indicate that aseko’s contribution deserves particular recognition because of the changes surrounding him. Di Salvo’s squad was missing several key midfield options, while the promotion of Tom Bischof to the senior national team and other withdrawals required the coach to assemble a revised central partnership.

Industry observers note that aseko consequently began both November fixtures alongside U21 debutant Cajetan Lenz. The pair faced an interesting challenge against Belgium. Germany wanted to press aggressively, regain possession high up the pitch, and support the attacking players through quick combinations. This frequently required the midfielders to advance into dangerous areas, leaving the defensive unit with considerable responsibility when the Belgians escaped pressure.

Sources indicate that aseko demonstrated his ability to carry possession forward as early as the sixth minute, accelerating past several Belgian opponents before combining with Brunner. His physical approach also produced an early yellow card, but the midfielder continued participating energetically in Germany’s attacking and defensive work. The partnership with Lenz was particularly encouraging.

Aseko contributed greater physicality and direct running, while his Hoffenheim colleague frequently assumed responsibility for progressing possession and connecting with the attacking players. In the Croatia match, with the playing surface progressively deteriorating, Aseko and Lenz were frequently required to abandon conventional passing combinations in favor of more direct and physically demanding actions.

Aseko nevertheless remained involved in Germany’s second-half revival. Immediately after the restart, the midfielder found himself in a shooting position following a corner, although his effort was blocked before reaching goal. His work helped Germany establish the territorial advantage that eventually produced Moerstedt’s equalizer and Pejcinovic’s second goal.

Sources indicate that aseko departed in the 64th minute, having again supplied an energetic performance despite the increasingly difficult conditions. Aseko continues to demonstrate why he deserves consideration for a regular place in that system. There are flashier candidates for an international-break winners list, but two strong performances alongside a newly introduced midfield partner merit recognition.

Recent findings suggest that the sixth and final inclusion requires a little explanation. Pejcinovic received a disappointing 4/10 rating from GGFN against Belgium, having struggled to impose himself consistently on the match. He nevertheless followed that performance with a considerably more encouraging display in Croatia, earning an 8/10 after scoring Germany’s second goal and producing several other noteworthy attacking contributions.

It has been revealed that the contrast is interesting, particularly when considered alongside Di Salvo’s assessment of the Belgium encounter. Pejcinovic had already enjoyed an excellent qualification campaign before November. As GGFN documented following Germany’s decisive victory over Georgia, the Stuttgart professional scored twice to help secure direct qualification for next summer’s European Championship.

Industry observers note that his transfer from Wolfsburg to Stuttgart earlier in the season also represented an important step in his professional development. As the striker acknowledged in an October interview , however, establishing himself at Bundesliga level for his new club has presented challenges.

Sources indicate that the November friendlies provided another opportunity to demonstrate his qualities. Against Belgium, Pejcinovic sometimes struggled with his timing and final deliveries. An attempted pass to Anton Kade early in the second half was particularly inaccurate, while his involvement in Germany’s attacking moves did not always translate into threatening opportunities.

Industry observers note that there were nevertheless positive contributions. Pejcinovic helped initiate the 58th-minute sequence in which Brunner released Damar for another attempt against the crossbar. His movement and willingness to participate in combinations also provided Germany with an additional presence between midfield and attack.

Di Salvo was keen to emphasize these aspects when asked about the striker’s performance at the post-match press conference.

It has been revealed that “No, that thought didn’t occur to me at all,” Di Salvo answered when questioned by the Rheinische Post about Dzenan Pejcinovic’s comparatively tepid performance on Friday night. “He trained strongly and scored his goals.”.

“We found him to be confident in the goal-shooting drills,” Di Salvo continued. “And we found the distance covered stats from not just Dzenan but the entire team today to be exceptionally good.”.

“He was always running and strong on the press,” Di Salvo concluded. “That’s what I judge to be most important. That was good. He participated in the build up play in the first half and was able to help out the play on the wings. We found that well-executed by the entire team.”.

Industry observers note that the coach’s comments provide a useful reminder that the assessment of an attacking player cannot rest exclusively upon his finishing or goalscoring contributions. Against Croatia, Pejcinovic offered considerably more of both.

Sources indicate that an excellent opportunity went begging in the 18th minute after Damar released him into space, but the Stuttgart forward continued working energetically despite the difficult playing conditions. His perseverance was rewarded after Germany’s halftime adjustments.

With Brunner operating from the left and Moerstedt providing an additional penalty-area presence, Pejcinovic found himself benefiting from a more productive attacking structure. The Stuttgart professional finished Brunner’s cross in the 60th minute to give Germany a 2-1 lead.

Further contributions followed at both ends of the pitch. Pejcinovic helped defend two Croatian corners at the near post and continued seeking opportunities to threaten the opposition goal. His excellent shot from distance in the 82nd minute forced Toni Silic into a save, with the rebound presenting Lenz with an opportunity to equalize before Croatia’s eventual winning goal.

The 8/10 GGFN rating reflected a much more complete attacking performance.

Pejcinovic remains an important member of Germany’s U21 squad, and November demonstrated both the value of his established attacking qualities and the considerable benefits of playing alongside forwards capable of complementing his movement.

Germany’s November international break offered plenty of interesting tactical material, even if the extraordinary conditions in Croatia necessarily limit how much one should attempt to extract from the second fixture. Di Salvo’s personnel difficulties were particularly significant.

Recent findings suggest that the absence of Tresoldi removed an established attacking reference point, while injuries and senior national-team promotions required substantial changes to the midfield and forward positions. The result was a Germany side that retained some familiar attacking principles but frequently looked different from the one that had secured European Championship qualification in October.

In a recent development, germany began the Belgium encounter in a nominal 4-2-3-1, with Brunner leading the line, Damar operating from the left, Kade on the right, and Pejcinovic occupying the central attacking position behind the striker. Lenz and Aseko formed the central midfield pairing.

The basic structure proved rather fluid. Damar frequently moved away from his starting position, seeking possession in central areas and occasionally appearing on the right. Brunner and Pejcinovic also pushed together into advanced positions, temporarily giving the formation the appearance of a more conventional 4-4-2. The central midfielders were encouraged to advance and participate in Germany’s attempts to recover possession high up the pitch.

These movements helped produce several encouraging attacking sequences. The problem, unfortunately, concerned the spaces Germany left behind whenever Belgium managed to escape the initial press. Julien Duranville’s eighth-minute opener demonstrated the danger. Lucas Stassin beat Collins on the right and supplied the delivery that allowed Duranville to finish from close range.

The hosts subsequently established greater territorial control, but their commitment to attacking occasionally invited further Belgian opportunities. Collins’ misplaced pass in the 44th minute nearly produced another goal, with Stassin ultimately striking the post.

Di Salvo’s team appeared somewhat more cautious after the restart, although Damar’s movement and individual initiative continued to generate threatening situations. The final result nevertheless reflected Germany’s difficulties in balancing attacking ambition with defensive protection.

Belgium’s second goal arrived immediately after both coaches made several substitutions, with the German defensive structure unable to respond quickly enough to a newly introduced attacker. Di Salvo subsequently praised his team’s pressing at the post-match press conference but acknowledged that the defending and missed opportunities had not been good enough.

The Croatia encounter was considerably more difficult to assess. Di Salvo made just one starting change, replacing Collins with Linus Gechter in central defence. Poor visibility made the precise opening formation difficult to determine, although Germany appeared to operate in a narrow 4-2-2-2.

The narrow attacking shape may have been influenced by the extraordinary circumstances. Thick fog made it difficult for players to locate teammates, while standing water increasingly disrupted attempts to circulate possession through the wider areas. The Germans initially attempted to play through the conditions, with mixed results.

Damar’s excellent pass to Pejcinovic in the 18th minute created a clear opportunity, but Croatia subsequently took the lead through Adrian Segecic. The most vital tactical development occurred at halftime. Di Salvo introduced Moerstedt, Collins, Morgalla, and Rothe. The changes allowed Brunner to move onto the left while Moerstedt assumed a more pronounced central attacking role.

Industry observers note that lineup—Germany U21 vs. Croatia (46th minute).

Industry observers note that the adjustment immediately improved Germany’s attacking options. Moerstedt supplied the penalty-area presence necessary to capitalize upon deliveries and loose balls, while Brunner became considerably more influential when attacking from the left.

Lenz’s involvement in the equalizer illustrated the continued importance of Germany’s midfielders in supporting attacks, while Brunner’s cross for Pejcinovic’s goal demonstrated the increased productivity of the revised attacking arrangement.

The hosts’ subsequent equalizer, scored after the ball became stranded in a large puddle, served as another reminder that conventional tactical analysis has its limitations when the conditions become this extreme.

In a recent development, the most encouraging developments concern Germany’s attacking options. Brunner demonstrated his versatility, Damar reaffirmed his attacking quality, and Moerstedt made an excellent initial case for a more substantial role in the U21 squad.

Pejcinovic remains a productive striker who can contribute beyond goalscoring, while Lenz and Aseko supplied an encouraging central midfield partnership despite the absence of several established alternatives.

The November defeats should not be dismissed, particularly given the defensive shortcomings that were evident against Belgium. Yet neither should the individual developments be overlooked.

Germany have already qualified for next summer’s European Championship, and Di Salvo now has several more footballers who have demonstrated that they deserve consideration when the competition for tournament places intensifies.

Two defeats, six winners, and more than a few selection headaches.

Not necessarily the conclusion to the international year one might have hoped for.

But certainly not a complete waste of time, either.

Dino Toppmöller, who left his role at French Ligue 1 side RC Lens in September, has been linked with a possible move back to the Bundesliga according to Sport BILD.

Cologne who only gathered nine points from the first nine games of the Bundesliga are contemplating a managerial change and the former Eintracht Frankfurt coach is on top of the list.

Toppmöller was dismissed from his role at Lens not because of results on the pitch but because of his loyalty to his assistant coach, whom he felt was wrongly terminated.

The Billy Goats will face Bayern Munich on Friday, but the next game against Elversberg on November 28 is expected to determine the future of 38-year-old coach Wagner.

Industry observers note that toppmöller was under consideration in Cologne last summer, but an agreement wasn’t reached on his salary. According to Sport Bild, the 45-year-old would be open to renewed talks. In addition to Toppmöller, Christian Eichner (most recently at Karlsruhe), Horst Steffen (most recently at Werder Bremen) and David Hubert (Union Saint-Gilloise) are possible candidates for the role if Wagner departs.
